count/filter: Count what a conv layer learns. One filter over a color image is three by three in each of three channels: twenty seven weights.
count/bias: Plus one bias, added after the sum. Twenty eight numbers per filter.
count/k: With eight filters, that is eight times twenty eight: two hundred and twenty four.
count/formula: In general: K, times F times F times C, plus one. Forget the C and you have counted a flat filter; forget the one and you have lost the biases.
shared/reuse: Notice what is missing: the image size. The same two hundred and twenty four numbers are used at every position. A bigger image is more work, but not more parameters.
shared/fc: Compare a fully connected layer, like a linear classifier, from the same image to the same output, eight by thirty by thirty. Every output has its own weight for every input: about twenty two million.
shared/why: Sharing one small filter across the image is what makes convolution cheap. It also builds in a belief: a pattern worth finding in one place is worth finding everywhere.
